Lessons: what broke while the brain was built, and the rule each one left

Read this before you change the setup, and when something looks wrong. Each lesson happened on the reference setup (2026-10-08 and 2026-10-09) and cost real time. Each one is written as symptom → cause → fix → rule. The fix is already in this repository's code or scripts unless the lesson says otherwise; the rule is what you must keep doing.

1. A move across the two path spellings copies instead of renaming

  • Symptom. A probe mv from /home/<devbox-user>/… to /Users/<user>/… on the devbox did not rename. It started to copy byte by byte.
  • Cause. /Users/<user> is a bind mount of /home/<devbox-user>. The kernel treats the two spellings as two mounts, so rename() between them fails with EXDEV (cross-device link). mv then falls back to copy + delete. For a 528 GB docs folder that is hours of copying and a delete at the end.
  • Fix. The devbox swap spelled source AND target under one spelling (/home/<devbox-user>/…), so it was one atomic rename in one process (rmdir + rename + symlink, about 10 µs apart).
  • Rule. On the devbox, every mv of a big tree spells both paths the same way. Check first with stat -c %d <source> <target-parent> (same device number). Never move across the two spellings.

2. The git snapshot hashed all of work/

  • Symptom. The 13:00 dream's snapshot step ran for a long time and ~/brain/.git grew fast.
  • Cause. The snapshot ran git add -A over the brain root. work/ holds about 600 GB of results on the devbox, and git started to hash all of it into .git.
  • Fix. The git process was stopped by PID. The brain's .gitignore now tracks only CARD.md under work/ (/work/*, !/work/*/, /work/*/*, !/work/*/CARD.md). .git went from 6.4 GB to 5.7 MB.
  • Rule. Git history covers brain text only. Never widen the brain's .gitignore to include box contents.

3. Unison: bulk, the 2 MB limit, half-copies, and a "dry run" that was live

  • Symptom A. The first Unison "dry run" copied files. Symptom B. Each sync prints hundreds of "skipped: would transfer a file of size greater than maxsizethreshold" lines. Symptom C. brain doctor on the laptop went red two hours after a sync, on files named .unison.*. Symptom D (2026-10-10). Conflict copies of files that only one machine wrote, after the laptop moved to a different network.
  • Cause A. -noupdate on both roots still CREATES new files. Cause B. By design: the sync carries text up to 2 MB (-maxsizethreshold 2048, in KB); bulk stays on the machine that made it (the boxes hold ~600 GB on the devbox and ~220 GB on the laptop). Cause C. An interrupted sync leaves Unison temp files behind. Cause D. Unison names its archive after the local hostname. macOS changes the laptop's hostname with the network, so the devbox had two archives (~/.unison/ar*), one for each name. After a change, the sync used the other, older archive, and a file that changed after that archive was written read as changed on both replicas.
  • Fix. brain sync --dry-run sets -nocreation -noupdate -nodeletion on both replicas (proven by a probe file that was skipped). Bulk folders (artifacts, .venv, node_modules, …) and everything but text under work/ are ignored. Every sync archives a .unison.* file older than 2 h (config.UnisonTempGrace). brain sync runs Unison with UNISONLOCALHOSTNAME set to the machine name. The first sync with a new name has no archive, so each file that is different on the two replicas at that time becomes a conflict copy, one time only.
  • Rule. Skip lines are normal; read brain sync status for the exit, not the scrollback. Put results that must reach the other machine in a text file, or copy a box on purpose with brain agents box. Never run Unison with -watch (editors already crawl these trees). Run Unison only through brain sync: a manual run uses the hostname and makes a second archive.

4. A link that loops back into work/ arrived by sync

  • Symptom. work/<old-docs-name> appeared on the devbox: a symlink pointing back at the old path, which now resolved into work/ itself.
  • Cause. The laptop still had a compat link inside the tree; Unison carried it over.
  • Fix. The link moved to .archive/cutover/stray-links/. brain doctor has a check, brain.work-root: no .git and no link back into the brain at the top of work/.
  • Rule. Never put a link to the brain inside the brain. Keep compat links outside ~/brain.

5. launchd jobs hang on ~/Documents (TCC)

  • Symptom. A bridge step that walked ~/Documents/… sat at 0 bytes for 3 minutes. A 1-second sample showed one thread in __open the whole time. It never failed; it just waited.
  • Cause. macOS privacy control (TCC) guards ~/Documents. A process started by launchd (the bridge, any LaunchAgent) has no terminal to show the permission prompt, so open() blocks forever instead of failing.
  • Fix. The job was stopped by PID and run again from an interactive laptop terminal, which TCC allows. The brain lives at ~/brain, outside ~/Documents, so its own jobs never hit this.
  • Rule. Laptop steps that read under ~/Documents (moving old doc folders in, manifests of them) run from an interactive terminal, never through the bridge or a LaunchAgent. Keep ~/brain outside ~/Documents.

6. The claude CLI hangs under launchd

  • Symptom. brain install on the laptop hung when the bridge ran it. A related case: after a launchd job ran claude -p, interactive sessions skipped an MCP server for 15 minutes.
  • Cause. The claude CLI waits on things launchd cannot give it (the keychain, a full PATH with node). Claude Code also caches MCP connect failures in one file that every session shares, so one failed launchd run spoils the others.
  • Fix. brain doctor checks Claude Code by reading its plugin registry and settings files, not by running claude. Paid model steps on the laptop run from an interactive shell (BRAIN_LLM_LOGIN=1). The brain's own model calls pass --strict-mcp-config or --bare, so they load no MCP servers.
  • Rule. Never run the claude CLI from launchd. If you must, set PATH to include node and pass --strict-mcp-config. If an interactive session lost a server, run /mcp and reconnect.

7. MEMORY.md was cut at 24.4 KB

  • Symptom. Claude Code printed a truncation warning, and rules at the end of memory/MEMORY.md never reached sessions.
  • Cause. Claude Code loads only about 24.4 KB of MEMORY.md and cuts the rest, whatever the line count.
  • Fix. The render cap is 200 lines AND 24 KiB (config.MemoryIndexMaxBytes). Lines are ordered so standing rules come first; a new rule that supersedes an old one takes its predecessor's place in the render. Each line carries the fact itself, not a description of it (a line that only describes needs a tool call to be useful).
  • Rule. Never edit MEMORY.md by hand; the dream renders it. Watch its size in brain doctor (graph caps).

8. SQLITE_BUSY_SNAPSHOT on the dream's reindex

  • Symptom. The 00:00 dream's reindex step failed with SQLite error 517 (SQLITE_BUSY_SNAPSHOT).
  • Cause. A hook committed to the index between the reindex's read and its write. A deferred transaction cannot upgrade from a stale read snapshot, so SQLite refused it at once.
  • Fix. Write transactions now begin IMMEDIATE (a test failed first). A failed dream step writes its last line to the worker log.
  • Rule. Any new code that reads then writes the index opens its transaction IMMEDIATE.

9. The MCP tools answered nothing (tool-name prefix)

  • Symptom. brain_search and the other tools returned nothing in Claude Code, for a whole day, with no error.
  • Cause. Claude Code calls a mod tool as mcp__saahil-brain__brain_search. The mod looked up the bare name.
  • Fix. The mod strips only its own prefix. Another server's tool with the same short name (for example a company MCP's brain_search) stays theirs. Verified in a fresh session.
  • Rule. After any change to the mod, prove a tool call in a FRESH session, not in a running one (running sessions pick up the mod only at restart).

10. CARDs went stale

  • Symptom. A box's CARD said "nothing merged" while its STATE listed 10 merged PRs. Every session in that box got the stale CARD in its digest.
  • Cause. Only the backfill wrote CARDs; the hourly dream never refreshed them, although the design says it does. An earlier bug made every CARD look stale: the box's own CARD.md counted as its newest file.
  • Fix. The dream step curate.cards refreshes up to 4 CARDs per dream whose box has work ≥ 1 h newer than the CARD (Haiku, inside the $8 cap). CARD.md itself is not work. brain dream cards --dry-run shows what it would pick.
  • Rule. A baseline that a design says is kept current needs a step that keeps it current, and a dry run that shows it. Check new design claims against the dream's step list.

11. One rule, many copies; old rules contradicting new ones

  • Symptom. MEMORY.md held the same rule three times; one global rule contradicted a newer one; an agent found the conflict only from Claude Code's truncation warning.
  • Cause. Filing made about one note per old memory. The duplicate check caught byte copies only, and nothing checked global rules against each other.
  • Fix. The dream step curate.merge (Opus) finds duplicate groups and conflicts among current global notes. It keeps the newest note with every distinct fact of the group, supersedes the rest (never deletes), narrows a conflict when dates settle it, and queues a pair it cannot settle in .brain/owner-questions.jsonl. brain doctor shows how many questions wait. brain dream merge is a dry run.
  • Rule. Merge, don't copy. When a question waits, answer it (see OPERATIONS.md); the newer dated rule wins only when the dates differ.
  • Later (2026-10-11): a narrowing that never landed. For 12 dreams the merge narrowed the same lesson, and the applier refused it each time: "a lesson body is ≤ 300 chars". The narrowing line goes at the end of the older note's body. A lesson body holds at most 300 chars, and 108 of the 109 global lessons had no room for the line. The step stayed ok, and no metric counted the refusal. Fix: when the body has no room, the narrowing goes in the older note's related link to the newer note, as its why (Narrowed <date>: <why>). Each dream step record has a refused count, and brain metrics shows "dream units refused". Rule: a write that must fit a cap needs a second place to go. Count the units a step refused, not only the steps that failed.
  • Later (2026-10-12): the merge landed nothing at all. The fix above worked in a replay, but the three dreams of the next day still changed no merged note. Each dream hit its 50-edit cap in learn, file and curate.link, and the cap went first come, first served, so every curate.hubs, curate.merge, curate.cards and verify edit was held (96 edits; $10 of the day's $13.54 bought edits that never landed). The step reasons still said "5 files" and "refreshed 2". Fix: learn and file keep first claim (they use up their input); the five curation steps share what is left equally. A held edit is marked held, and brain metrics shows "dream edits held by the cap". Rule: a shared budget spent in a fixed order needs shares, or the last steps never run.
  • Later (2026-10-13): verify paid for fixes that could not land. The applier refused 109 of the 254 ops that verify proposed in its first 32 runs (43%), each for a cap: a summary over 160 chars, a lesson body over 300, a note over 4 KB. The verify skill named none of them, and its rule "append the reason" can never fit a lesson. So its status changes on lessons (retired, proposed) never landed, and it proposed the same ones again each run. "dream units refused" read 0, because only curate.merge counted refusals. Fix: verify states the caps and sets only the status of a lesson; every skill step counts its refused ops in refused; a test checks that each skill that writes note text states the three caps. Rule: a prompt that writes into a checked format states the checks, and a test keeps the two the same.

12. Evals that leak or misdate their targets

  • Symptom. Early navigation numbers looked better than real use felt. After the cut-over, the same evals dropped for no real reason.
  • Cause. Targets leaked: a file the session itself wrote counted as "found"; an echoed brief counted as a target; bulk folders counted; the ranking used the brain as of today, not as of the session. After the cut-over, dates, old path spellings and namesake folders confused the matcher.
  • Fix. A target must have existed before the session (birth time, mtime or an earlier session's touch); bulk is never a target; ranking runs as of the session's start; old spellings map to new paths. DEV is for tuning; TEST is run once. The headline eval is real: prompts you typed and the file that answered (brain eval build --human, Opus-judged, never storing prompt text).
  • Rule. Never edit eval sets, targets or marks to pass. Judge a change on TEST once, and on the owner-typed eval.

13. A path rewrite reset 15,340 file times

  • Symptom. After the cut-over's path rewrite, every rewritten file looked new, so every CARD looked stale and "newest file" logic broke.
  • Cause. The rewrite replaced files with new bytes and kept the new mtime.
  • Fix. brain cutover restore-mtimes put the old times back from the rewrite manifests (only on files unchanged since). rewrite-paths now keeps each file's mtime.
  • Rule. Any tool that rewrites files in place keeps their mtime. Moves (rename) keep mtimes for free; prefer a move to a copy.

14. Cost caps

  • Symptom (prevented). A loop or a retry storm in an unattended job can spend without limit.
  • Cause. Dreams, learning and the backfill call models with nobody watching.
  • Fix. Three caps in code: ≤ $8 per dream run (each step must fit its budget first: Opus $2.50, Haiku $0.50); ≤ $100 per UTC day for all brain model calls, failed attempts included; backfill ≤ $80 in total (--budget). Every answer is cached by an idempotency key, so a retry or rerun never pays twice. On the reference setup the most expensive dream cost $5.97, and the busiest 24 hours (backfill included) about $75.
  • Rule. Keep the caps. Raise the backfill --budget on purpose, not by removing the guard. Interactive and Orca agent sessions are not in this ledger.

15. A secrets guard blocks any command that names a secrets file

  • Symptom. On the reference laptop a guard mod refused commands, even a grep, that named a secrets file. An earlier probe had printed a key's prefix and hash.
  • Cause. Secrets files must never enter a conversation or a log; the guard blocks any command that names one.
  • Fix. The brain's file tools never open .env* files (rewrite-paths skips them unread), and setup takes credentials only through the tools that own them (SSO, the GitHub certificate flow).
  • Rule. Never open, print or copy a secrets file. Refer to them generically. Never print a key's prefix, length or hash.

16. Kill by PID, never by pattern

  • Symptom. pkill -f <pattern> killed the agent's own shell (exit 144). Wait loops on pgrep -f never ended.
  • Cause. An agent's Bash tool wraps each command in bash -c '<command>', so the pattern always matches a live process: the agent's own.
  • Fix. Stop a process by the PID a tool reported, or pick PIDs by an exact field match (ps -eo pid,args and test the program field).
  • Rule. Never pkill -f. Wait on a PID (while kill -0 $PID), a marker file or a log line.

17. One worktree per task

  • Symptom. Two tasks in one checkout mixed into one diff; a git checkout -b in a shared worktree moved another live session's checkout.
  • Cause. Agents start in whatever checkout they were launched in, often one that another session uses.
  • Fix. Each net-new task gets its own worktree off fresh origin/main (brain agents new does this through Orca). The daily care agent works the same way and removes its worktree and branch at the end.
  • Rule. One task, one worktree, removed when its branch lands. Never checkout -b inside a worktree you were launched in.

18. The dream reverted its own run

  • Symptom. A dream spent $3.78 and every edit was reverted.
  • Cause. The check step ran brain lint on brain-relative paths from another working folder, so lint failed (exit 2) and the safety net restored every file.
  • Fix. Dream commands run from the brain root, and lint resolves brain-relative paths. The cached answers made the rerun free.
  • Rule. The revert-on-lint-failure net works; keep it. A dream that reverts everything is a tooling bug, not a content bug: read the run report in .brain/dream-runs/ first.

19. A token in a transcript reached a session note

  • Symptom. A session note held a bare 43-character local MCP token from an old transcript.
  • Cause. The first redactor caught known key shapes only, not a bare high-entropy token.
  • Fix. The redactor redacts bare high-entropy tokens; every session note was rewritten; the token was purged from the brain's local git history; lint warns (never errors) on random-looking tokens, so a document id cannot revert a dream. The original transcript still held the token, so it had to be rotated at its source.
  • Rule. Treat any secret found in the brain as leaked: rotate it at the source, then clean the copies.

20. An unanchored ignore line hid code folders

  • Symptom. cmd/brain vanished from git status in the brain's code repo.
  • Cause. The global git ignore line brain (to keep brain links out of commits) also matched every folder named brain.
  • Fix. brain install writes the anchored form /brain (repo root only) and drops the old forms. A test pins it.
  • Rule. Anchor ignore lines that target one root entry.

21. A brain link in a repo can be uploaded or crawled

  • Symptom (found before it happened). gcloud builds submit from a work repo would have uploaded the whole brain. An editor's TypeScript server held 888k of 1.03M inotify watches by following an old docs link.
  • Cause. gcloud follows symlinks when it collects files, unless .gcloudignore names the link. Language servers and file watchers follow links too.
  • Fix. The reference setup keeps a brain link in every repo root (git-ignored by /brain) by the owner's choice. Agents do not need it: BRAIN.md is loaded everywhere and paths are absolute.
  • Rule. Before you add brain links to a repo, check that repo's upload tools (.gcloudignore, .dockerignore) and editor watchers. Never commit the link. Never edit a company repo's ignore files for the brain.

22. Claude Code refused a symlinked plugin

  • Symptom. The mod did not load when its folder was a symlink to the code repo.
  • Cause. Claude Code refuses plugin files that resolve outside their marketplace folder. A directory marketplace plugin also needs claude plugin install before it loads.
  • Fix. brain install writes the mod's files into the marketplace folder as ordinary files and runs claude plugin install for it.
  • Rule. Install the mod with brain install, not by linking.

23. agents move failed three ways before it worked

  • Symptom. Moving a laptop session to the devbox failed with selector_not_found, then stopped at a trust question, then aborted on one file.
  • Cause. Orca opens terminals only at a project root; a folder new to the devbox stops at Claude Code's workspace-trust question; the notes sync aborted on a file another build was writing.
  • Fix. move opens the Orca terminal at the project root and starts the session in its subfolder, pre-trusts the target folder, and tolerates a file in flight. Then it ran live: resumed with history, renamed, listed, stopped.
  • Rule. Prove a mesh command with a live run on a throwaway session before you rely on it.

24. devbox down said "already" when AWS failed

  • Symptom. With an expired AWS sign-in, devbox down printed already and exited 0. It stopped nothing.
  • Cause. The instance-state read returned an empty string on error, and the script treated it as a state.
  • Fix. A failed state read is fatal: the helper prints "cannot read the instance state", names the sign-in to renew, and exits 1. Tested with a stub aws on PATH, never against the real instance.
  • Rule. A helper that controls a machine fails loudly when it cannot read the machine. Test stop paths with stubs.

25. Moving a cited file turned doctor red

  • Symptom. brain doctor went red on both machines for 20 minutes after a test memory was moved to .archive/.
  • Cause. A filed note cited that memory as evidence, so the link dangled.
  • Fix. The memory went back.
  • Rule. Before you move a file out of the live tree, run brain show <path> and check what links to it.
  • Later (2026-10-12): code moved cited files too. A session note's file name held the session's name, and a /rename moved the note. Three renamed sessions left 103 dangling citations in 56 notes. The applier checks every path in a note it edits, so each later edit of those notes was refused, merges into them included. Fix: a session note keeps the path of its first write (a rename changes name:), and the applier moves a cited session path with an old slug onto the session's one note when it edits the note. An empty update_note delta repaired the 56 notes.

26. Gaps a fresh install exposed

The reference brain went through a shadow phase and a hand-run cut-over, on one person's machines. Packaging it for a new person showed steps that only ever happened by hand, and values that only fit the first owner:

  • The live marker. Nothing wrote ~/brain/.brain/live; it was written by hand at the cut-over. Without it the hooks stay in shadow (they log and inject nothing), brain install never sets Claude Code's autoMemoryDirectory, brain dream schedule defaults to shadow, and the backfill stages CARDs instead of writing them. Fix: brain init marks a fresh brain live when the marker is absent and shadow_docs is empty (a new brain has nothing to cut over). Check: cat ~/brain/.brain/live prints a UTC time.
  • The mod's marketplace. brain install wired the Claude Code mod only when the owner's local marketplace folder already existed and was registered with Claude Code. A new person has neither, so Claude Code would get the rules file and the mesh hooks but no digest, pointers, guard or brain_* tools. Fix: brain install creates ~/mods/saahil-mods/.claude-plugin/marketplace.json when it is missing, registers it, then installs the mod. Check: claude plugin list shows saahil-brain, and brain doctor shows host.claude … mod ✓ · loaded ✓.
  • The worker's model login. The worker ran claude --bare -p, which needs an API key, or a team wrapper (devbox-exec) that the first owner's devbox had. A systemd unit gets no shell profile, so on a new devbox the dream's model calls would fail auth. Fix: the brain-worker unit template sets BRAIN_LLM_LOGIN=1: the calls use the person's own Claude login on the devbox; no API key. Check: systemctl --user show brain-worker -p Environment contains BRAIN_LLM_LOGIN=1.
  • The care agent's notification. The care goal ended with a notifier command that only the first owner had installed. Fix: the notify step runs only when a notifier is installed; the report is the record either way.
  • Seed hubs and code defaults. The seed hubs were the first owner's topics, and code defaults held one team's SSO session, certificate path and PR repo. Fix: brain init seeds only generic hubs (the person adds their own domains); code defaults are generic; team values live in a team profile (profiles/<team>.json, kept out of git and built into the binary, merged by brain identity --init --profile <team>); personal values stay in the never-committed identity.json. The Makefile's dist path comes from settings, not a fixed home.
  • Rule. A step that ran by hand once is a step a new install will miss, and a value that fits one person is a bug for the next. Put the step in code with a check, and the value in settings.
